title: Perfect scalar transport along a ring isomorphism
statement: Let A and B be commutative rings and a : A ≅ B. For any fixed derived categories of their module categories, the full subcategories of perfect complexes [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex] are equivalent. The forward functor, followed by inclusion, is naturally isomorphic to inclusion followed by the fixed derived scalar extension [def-zl-ring-derived-scalar-extension] along a. No nonzero-ring or equal-localization-universe hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Restriction along mutually inverse ring maps gives exact inverse module functors. Apply the derived-category equivalence functor. A bounded finite-projective representative remains bounded, finite and projective: the identity underlying additive map is a semilinear equivalence and transports finite generation and projectivity. Apply this in both directions, using the unit isomorphism to reflect perfection.

Restrict the derived equivalence to perfect objects, which are closed under isomorphisms. Its forward functor and the fixed derived scalar extension are left adjoints to the same derived restriction. The unique left-adjoint isomorphism gives the required inclusion comparison.

proof_origin.reason: Explicit finite-projective representative transport used in HRS Proposition 4.3(3).
